The patient experienced no postoperative complications.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (a, b, c). a: 22-year-old male with right hypochondriac pain; panel-specific caption gall bladder (g) transverse plane plus disease-focused article title diagnosing acute acalculous cholecystitis due to Ascaris lumbricoides; visual linear worm in gallbladder lumen matching biliary worm ultrasound. b: Same patient longitudinal gallbladder view showing same echogenic worm structure; caption 'gall bladder (g)' plus ascariasis cholecystitis article title supports biliary ascariasis attribution. c: Small bowel loop sonogram in patient with intestinal ascariasis shows worm structures, but no vocabulary finding_key covers intestinal worm on ultrasound (only barium study, biliary ultrasound, ERCP); per rule 6 no vocabulary manifestation can be named so panel excluded, proposed as intestinal worm on ultrasound.

in_text_mentions: A 22-year-old male patient presented to our emergency department with two days' history of upper abdominal pain and fever. There was no history of jaundice. Clinical examination revealed tenderness in the right hypochondrium with mild guarding. There was no palpable mass. Ultrasonography of the abdomen in transverse and longitudinal planes and of one of the small bowel loops is shown in Figure 1. The biliary tree was normal.
